<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **18** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/webhook.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/security/_activation/webhook (route, a path literal in CATEGORY_LINES; a path literal in SWITCH_DOORS; a path literal in WEBHOOK_SWITCH_DOOR), /security/_activation/:type/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line), /security/_activation/webhook/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via /security/_activation/:type/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/email-service.mdx`  _(via callerPackageId (symbol, a field of const object base))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via /security/_activation/:type/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_
- `content/docs/permissions/sharing-rules.mdx`  _(via handleCatalogActivationWrite (symbol, a top-level function), /security/_activation/:type/:name (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/webhook.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **179** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 67274acad689d5be75d5bfc5007f4fb9396aa907` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cd5284edd0ae3a7da95c8ee8bb98e40128b1ce15` — the merge of head `0afa1e4627236ecff76807c9c4e81996d6c7c603` into base `67274acad689d5be75d5bfc5007f4fb9396aa907`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cd5284edd0ae3a7da95c8ee8bb98e40128b1ce15 && git checkout cd5284edd0ae3a7da95c8ee8bb98e40128b1ce15
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 67274acad689d5be75d5bfc5007f4fb9396aa907 0afa1e4627236ecff76807c9c4e81996d6c7c603 && git checkout -B drift-repro 67274acad689d5be75d5bfc5007f4fb9396aa907 && git merge --no-ff 0afa1e4627236ecff76807c9c4e81996d6c7c603

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 67274acad689d5be75d5bfc5007f4fb9396aa907
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 67274acad689d5be75d5bfc5007f4fb9396aa907` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

The PR head is still `c68c098f0`. The file list decides no review face; the changeset's `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line makes this the declaration face.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged:

1. `POST /security/_activation/webhook/NAME?package=PKG`, PKG serving NAME: FROM `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` TO `200`, PKG's own `(webhook, package_id, name)` row written, `data.packageId` in the answer. **Right.** `resolveExactWebhook` matches the served slots by exact package id only; nothing is inferred. Pinned in both registration orders (`catalog-activation-door.test.ts`), with the row naming no package left untouched under two holders.
2. Same address, PKG not serving NAME (a disabled package included): FROM `400` TO `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` `not-held-by-qualifier` naming the served holders, or `404` when nothing serves the name; nothing written. **Right**, and it is the refusal shape the namespace address already gives. Pinned.
3. One holder, `?package=` its own id: writes the row the bare address writes and adopts the row naming no package through the same `webhookAdoptsPackageless` count (every holder, disabled included) as the namespace arm. **Right** (D8 unchanged). Pinned as a CONTROL.
4. Closed query set: `package` alone on the webhook's bare address, none on `webhook/NS/NAME`, none on every other non-permission type; empty or repeated `package` is `400`. **Right** (route rule 5). Pinned, the namespace address and `sharing_rule` included.
5. Bare `webhook/NAME` and `webhook/NS/NAME` with no query: unchanged, still `409` naming both under two holders, in both orders. **Right** — red line 1 holds; red line 3 holds, since the only door answer that moves is a former `400`.
6. Upgrade-impact report, `withheldWebhooks`: FROM one finding (the holder the bare artifact lookup answers) TO one finding per holder, a disabled second holder included, each confirmed by `shipsAt`. **Right**, card item 6. The production registry carries `packageScopedHoldersOf` (the method is optional only for test doubles). The finding set's digest moves for a deployment in that state, so it is notified once more; that follows from the declared row.
7. Upgrade-impact report log lines (`SWITCH_DOORS`, withheld-webhook line): the namespace address replaced by `webhook/NAME?package=PACKAGE`, or the bare address for a finding naming no package. **Right as far as card item 5 asks**, with finding S2 below.
8. Exported surface of `@objectstack/runtime`: `WEBHOOK_DOOR_QUERY_PARAMS` added; `catalogActivationQueryParams` and `readPermissionSetPackageQuery` each gain one optional trailing parameter; `@objectstack/plugin-security`'s `UpgradeImpactRegistry` gains one optional method. **Right**: all additive, no existing caller changes meaning (`permission-set-clone.ts` reads the same message as before).
9. Checklist items `integration-system.webhook-lifecycle` steps[1] and `cli.organization-ownership-ceremony` acceptance[5].verify now expect `declared:com.example.showcase/showcase_task_changed`. **Right**: it is what `upgrade-18x-harness.dogfood.test.ts` pins for a fresh delivery; revisions and history bumped; the one remaining bare reference in `cli.json` is a dated history entry and correctly stays.
10. `packages/spec/liveness/webhook.json` `name` evidence, the `route-ledger.ts` note and `content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx`: prose only, each agrees with the code read. **Right.**
11. Card items 2 and 8: pins only, no answer moves. **Right** (`B disabled beside A enabled` is `409` naming A; one holder with its own row beside a row naming no package writes its own row).

Findings (none is a must-fix):

- **S1 · should-fix.** Card item 1 names three states; the pins build one (two co-owners of one namespace). The state the PR title and changeset also claim, a package that declares no namespace beside another holder, has no pin for `?package=` or for both holders being dispatched. The code read is namespace-agnostic, so no defect is read; the claim is simply unpinned.
- **S2 · should-fix.** Items 5 and 6 meet badly: the report now emits a finding for a DISABLED holder and its line sends the operator to `?package=PACKAGE`, which this PR's own pin answers `409` for a disabled package. The PR body's "every packaged finding can use" is therefore overstated. Not a regression (on `main` the namespace address refused the disabled holder too), so text or a follow-up, not a blocker.
- **N1 · nit.** `catalog-activation.ts` module doc still reads "`package` for `permission`, nothing for every other type", which the paragraph added a few lines below contradicts.
- **N2 · nit.** `WithheldDeclaredWebhook.packageId` is always a string, so "a finding that names no package" cannot occur on the withheld-webhook line; the clause is true only of the shared `SWITCH_DOORS` line.
- **N3 · nit.** The changeset's first FROM/TO row does not mention `data.packageId` in the `200` (the PR body does).

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` stand line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset, and they agree. **Correct.**
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is the right derivation: the diff adds nothing a metadata author can write (no key, value or type); a query parameter on an HTTP door is not authorable metadata. The claim's expected `added` was a forecast, and the diff does not bear it out.
- `(widening)` is right: the only moved door answers are former `400`s; nothing that answered `2xx`, `404` or `409` on `main` answers differently. No BREAKING banner or ADR-0087 marker is owed.
- Level: `none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. `@objectstack/runtime: patch` and `@objectstack/plugin-security: patch` match what the diff publishes from each.
- Nit N4: `packages/spec/liveness/` is in `@objectstack/spec`'s published `files`, and the evidence text changes, but `@objectstack/spec` is not named in the changeset. The fixed version group bumps it with the others, so only its changelog line is missing. `Check Changeset` concluded success.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev `open_questions`: empty. Nothing to answer.
- Deviation, file surface: `packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts` and `content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx`, one sentence each, declared in the PR body as extended by the seat. Both are accurate and needed by the new address. **Accepted**; the seat's own extension message is not among this review's inputs, so the seat confirms it.
- Deviation, `Metadata-protocol` derived `none` against the claim's `added`: **answered in ②, agreed.**
- Deviation, card item 7 not in the PR: the PR says a security item is with the owner seat. Not reviewed here. The PR says `Refs`, not `Closes`, so the card stays open for it. **Accepted.**
- Out-of-scope finding carried by the dev (plugin-webhooks' own remedies, `declaredWebhookActivationPath`, still name the namespace address, which answers `409` for two co-owners): **escalated to the seat.** Now that a door exists that switches those holders, a remedy that names one that refuses is the same defect card item 5 fixed in the report; it is a ruled text, so it needs a follow-up card, not an edit here.
- **Escalated to the seat**, with S2: decide whether a disabled holder's finding should name a door at all.
- **Escalated to the seat**, as a question: the environment's own declaration beside a packaged holder of the same name has no package id for `?package=` to name. The card does not list that state and this review did not establish how the bare address answers it; if it is `409`, that holder still has no switch.
- Claim line "Contract review: this seat, at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`": the committed tree touches no published schema and no governed path (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` success), so the review owed is the declaration face at `TIER_DEFAULT`, as rendered here.

Check-runs on `c68c098f0` (45): 17 success, 9 skipped, 0 failed, 19 still running.
- Success: Auto Label, Dogfood Regression Gate, Plan Test Core shards, Plan Test UI shards, filter, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Type Check · source gates, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check PR Size, Check Documentation Links, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Flag docs affected by code changes.
- Skipped: the Dogfood Regression Gate matrix row, Temporal Conformance, UI Published Artifacts, Dogfood Verify CLI, Schedule gate, Packed-tarball smoke, Borrowed queue verdict, Queue verdict, 18.x upgrade harness.
- Still running, not judged: Test Core (1/8) to (8/8), Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · consumer gates, Lint · CI, release and engine gates, Lint · scoped · slot lookup and corpus, Lint · repo and tooling gates, Lint · docs and code guards.
